_about: Pure fuel components and the fuel grades in the catalogue. Component properties are handbook values (Heywood, Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, 2nd ed., table D.4; ASTM/EN 228 typical gasoline). Blends are computed in engine.js: energy, stoichiometry and heat of vaporisation by mass, octane linear in molar fraction (Anderson et al., SAE 2012-01-1274). Pump gasoline in the EU already contains up to 5-10 % ethanol; the 'gasoline' component here is the ethanol-free base.

gasoline.source: typical EN 228 hydrocarbon base; RON/MON set per grade

ethanol.source: Heywood table D.4; neat-ethanol RON/MON from Anderson et al. 2012

race_hc.source: leaded/oxygen-free race fuel class (C16-type): modeled from published RON/MON typicals

ron95.label: Euro 95 (E5)
ron95.note: base chosen so the E5 blend lands at 95 RON / ~85 MON

ron98.label: Euro 98 (E5)
ron98.note: E5 blend lands at 98 RON / ~87 MON

blend_wmi.label: 98 + E20-blend (+ WMI hardware)
blend_wmi.note: 98 base with about 20 % ethanol; water-methanol comes from the WMI kit

e85.label: E85
e85.note: EN 15293 E85 is 70-85 % ethanol depending on season

flex.label: Flex (ethanolsensor)
flex.note: ethanol content set in the tune (E0-E100) and measured by the flex sensor
